note: Official POST /order, POST /orders and DELETE /orders response contracts. Read from the pinned clob-openapi.yaml (sha256 82529177635db366c31a08777355b4b95c392a427298c3ba68904b937d4594da, unchanged since the 2026-08-23 pin). Nothing here is derived from this SDK's Java code.

transactionsHashes.description: Array of transaction hashes (present when status is 'matched')

sendOrderResponse.settlementContradiction: constraints.json settlement (changelog Jul 17, 2026) says POST /order returns tradeIDs INSTEAD OF transactionHashes. The live clob-openapi.yaml still documents transactionsHashes on SendOrderResponse and still shows it in the matched_order and mixed_results examples. Both are official. Carry the field when present rather than dropping a documented success field; never require it.

postOrdersResponse.shape: array of SendOrderResponse, one element per submitted order
postOrdersResponse.note: The array carries no per-item request ID, so an element can only be attributed by position.

cancelOrdersResponse.canceled: array of order IDs that were successfully canceled
cancelOrdersResponse.notCanceled: object mapping order ID to the server's reason string
cancelOrdersResponse.duplicateHandling: Duplicate order IDs in the request are automatically ignored.
cancelOrdersResponse.silenceIsNotAnAnswer: No official text says an ID absent from BOTH canceled and not_canceled was not canceled. The published examples always account for every requested ID. An unmentioned ID is unaccounted for, not a stated refusal.

sources: https://docs.polymarket.com/api-spec/clob-openapi.yaml (DELETE /orders body: array of type string, no item pattern)

evidence.noPattern: Every orderID / order_id / order_ids field in clob-openapi.yaml is a bare `type: string`. Sibling fields in the same schemas DO carry patterns (maker_address ^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$, market ^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{64}$), so the omission is deliberate, not an oversight.
evidence.emptyIsDocumented: POST /orders per-item failure examples carry orderID: '' — an absent identifier, not an identifier of some other shape.

orderIdentifierSyntax.commonShape: Every non-empty official order-ID example matches ^0x[0-9a-fA-F]+$. Only the LENGTH disagrees (40 vs 64 hex), so the length must not be enforced.
orderIdentifierSyntax.verdict: Enforce the 0x-hex shape locally, never a length. The spec publishes no pattern, so anything stricter than the shape every official example shares would be invented.
